headline: Ethereum XAUt is owned by a 3-of-6 Tether multisig that can immediately mint, blocklist, burn blocked balances, and exercise token-owner powers; proxy-admin slot was not successfully read.

findings.text: Ethereum owner() at block 25064190 returns 0xC6CDE7C39eB2f0F0095F41570af89eFC2C1Ea828; that address has six owners and required() = 3.
Ethereum XAUt is a TransparentUpgradeableProxy to implementation 0x4C0d2c74a8d26f1e4f5653021c521f5471f9e566; explorer/ABI expose changeAdmin, upgradeTo, and upgradeToAndCall.
Evidenced fast path is 3 multisig confirmations then executeTransaction; no timelock/governor delay constant was found on that path.
Reachable control multisig is 3-of-6; signer identities were not verified, so it does not meet the Security Council standard.
No Governor/GovernorBravo/OZ Governor/Aragon Voting contract was identified in the fetched path.
No separate pause guardian was identified; emergency-like powers are owner-operated blocklist/burn controls.
Highest evidenced tier is T1: owner can mint, blocklist, and burn blocked balances; proxy upgrade functions can replace token logic if the proxy-admin path is controlled by the same apparatus.

steelman.red: The same privileged apparatus can mint, blocklist, burn blocked funds, and potentially upgrade token logic with no evidenced user exit window.
steelman.orange: The directly evidenced actor is a 3-of-6 multisig, not a single EOA or 2-of-3, but it fails Security Council criteria and has no evidenced timelock.
steelman.green: Green would require T1 to be unreachable, delayed at least seven days through broad governance, or guarded by a qualifying Security Council; none was shown.

rationale.verdict: Choosing orange because T1 token-owner powers are reachable through a 3-of-6 multisig with no evidenced timelock, which fails green, while the fetched evidence does not prove a single EOA or 2-of-3 path that would force red.

evidence.shows: Ethereum proxy surfacer: TransparentUpgradeableProxy, implementation, owner, totalSupply, and write methods including addToBlockedList, destroyBlockedFunds, mint, redeem, changeAdmin, upgradeTo, upgradeToAndCall.
owner() at block 25064190 returns 0xC6CDE7C39eB2f0F0095F41570af89eFC2C1Ea828.
Multisig owners at block 25064190: six owner addresses.
required() at block 25064190 is 3.
Etherscan proxy page shows current implementation and transparent-proxy admin/upgrade ABI.
Protocol info: XAUt provides ownership of real physical gold; TVL by chain; TVL = total XAUt minted.
Tether bug-bounty / disclosure page.

unknowns: C1: Arbitrum/Polygon live owner/admin reads were not completed; proxy-only surfacers did not expose zero-arg owner reads and direct read-API URLs were rejected by the fetch allowlist.
C2: EIP-1967 proxy admin slot was not successfully read for Ethereum, Arbitrum, or Polygon.
C3: if an external proxy-admin timelock exists, it was not verified.
C4: multisig signer identities and insider/non-insider status were not verified.
C5: voting threshold, voting period, quorum, and queue delay are unknown because no governor was identified.
C6: maximum duration/scope documentation for blocklist/burn powers was not found.

protocol_metadata.about: Tether Gold (XAUt) is a tokenized gold asset: DeFiLlama describes it as ownership of real physical gold, and the Ethereum contract is an ERC-20-like XAUt token. Users transfer XAUt on-chain, while issuance/redemption against gold is issuer-operated; Ethereum is an upgradeable proxy and L2 deployments expose OFT-style cross-chain mint/burn.

headline: There is no permissionless on-chain redemption to the underlying asset; transfers can be blocked indefinitely and blocked balances can be burned by the owner multisig.

findings.text: User-facing movement is transfer/transferFrom/multiTransfer. redeem(uint256) exists but is onlyOwner and burns from owner(), so it is not a permissionless holder exit.
transferFrom is onlyNotBlocked; _beforeTokenTransfer blocks transfers from blocked accounts unless msg.sender is owner; redeem/mint/blocklist/burn are onlyOwner.
The pause-equivalent guard is owner-controlled isBlocked; no maximum block duration was found, and destroyBlockedFunds burns a blocked balance.
No distinct time-capped emergency pause versus governance pause was identified; blocklist/burn uses the owner path.
No on-chain queued-redemption system, maximum queue duration, or daily cap was found.
No forced-exit or permissionless emergency withdrawal was found for a blocked holder or unprocessed redemption.
Direct on-chain token calls are possible through explorer write tabs/generic wallets, but that does not create permissionless gold redemption.

steelman.red: A holder has no permissionless on-chain redemption and can be indefinitely blocked from transferring, after which the owner can burn the balance.
steelman.orange: Unblocked holders can still transfer on-chain without the official frontend, so secondary-market exit works until blocklisting.
steelman.green: Green would require permissionless exit or tightly capped pause powers and non-paused finalized claims; the fetched code shows neither.

rationale.verdict: Choosing red because the only redemption-named on-chain function is owner-only, transfers are subject to an uncapped owner-controlled blocklist, and blocked funds can be destroyed.

evidence.shows: Ethereum surfacer lists transfer/transferFrom plus privileged addToBlockedList, removeFromBlockedList, destroyBlockedFunds, mint, and redeem.
Implementation source shows onlyNotBlocked, isBlocked, owner-only blocklist functions, owner-only redeem/mint, and destroyBlockedFunds burning blocked balances.
Privileged owner is 0xC6CDE7C39eB2f0F0095F41570af89eFC2C1Ea828 at block 25064190.
Explorer exposes direct Read/Write and Read/Write as Proxy tabs for on-chain calls.
Protocol info: XAUt provides ownership of real physical gold; TVL by chain; TVL = total XAUt minted.
Tether bug-bounty / disclosure page.

unknowns: E1: gold-specific off-chain redemption terms from gold.tether.to/faq and gold.tether.to/legal/termsofservice could not be extracted because those pages returned JavaScript-only shells.
E3: no PAUSE_ROLE/GUARDIAN role was found; role-style hasRole/getRoleAdmin reads were not applicable to the fetched Ownable blocked-list code.
E4: off-chain redemption suspension rules were not reconstructed from gold-specific terms.
E5: any off-chain redemption queue maximum duration remains unverified.
E6: no separate recovery/escape-hatch contract was identified.
E7: direct callability of off-chain redemption was not applicable because redemption against gold was not found as a permissionless on-chain flow.

headline: Worst-unmitigated dependency can affect ~100% of TVS: XAUt is a claim on off-chain physical gold, and L2 XAUt0 adds mutable OFT mint/burn dependencies with no verified fallback.

findings.text: No reserve/price oracle call was found on the Ethereum surfacer; the material dependency is the off-chain gold/issuer process. L2 contracts add an external oftContract authorized for mint/burn.
DeFiLlama describes XAUt as ownership of real physical gold and TVL as minted XAUt; the fetched contracts do not prove vault custody, allocation, or reserve solvency.
Arbitrum/Polygon deployments expose OFT-style crosschainMint/crosschainBurn; failure of the configured OFT/messaging path can affect L2 supply.
No nested on-chain collateral chain was found; the nested asset is off-chain physical gold/custody, whose failure propagates to XAUt economic value.
The fetched DeFiLlama page did not show a fork lineage; no fork dependency was identified.
No live on-chain fallback, reserve sanity check, second oracle, or circuit breaker was found that keeps holders whole after reserve/custody or OFT failure.
No protocol-owned L2/L3/appchain sequencer was identified; listed L2s are treated as third-party chain substrate.
Plain transfers need no keeper; cross-chain mint/burn liveness/correctness depends on the configured OFT/messaging path.
The external dependency surface is owner-mutable on L2: setOFTContract(address) is onlyOwner and changes the contract authorized to mint/burn cross-chain supply.

steelman.red: The core asset depends on external gold/custody and L2 supply depends on mutable OFT endpoints; worst-case dependency failure can impair principal across effectively all XAUt TVS.
steelman.orange: The ERC-20 transfer layer is simple, and OFT risk is small relative to Ethereum TVL, so some external failures are bounded to non-Ethereum deployments.
steelman.green: Green would require no material external dependency or live fallbacks that keep users whole, which was not evidenced.

rationale.verdict: Choosing red because the worst unmitigated dependency is the off-chain physical-gold/issuer/custody layer behind the minted-token TVL, and the contracts expose no on-chain mechanism that keeps holders whole if that external layer fails; L2 OFT dependencies are also owner-mutable.

evidence.shows: Protocol info, TVL $3.359b, Ethereum $3.332b, chain split, ownership-of-real-physical-gold description, and TVL=minted XAUt methodology.
Ethereum token/proxy surfacer with owner-controlled mint/redeem/blocklist/burn and no reserve-oracle reads surfaced.
Arbitrum source defines oftContract, onlyAuthorizedSender, crosschainMint/crosschainBurn, and onlyOwner setOFTContract.
Polygon implementation ABI includes crosschainMint, crosschainBurn, oftContract, setOFTContract, mint, redeem, and blocklist methods.
Tether legal terms evidence issuer-operated eligibility, freezes, blacklists, and service restrictions; used as corroboration, not as gold-specific terms.
Tether bug-bounty / disclosure page.

unknowns: A1: exhaustive grep of every listed-chain deployment was not completed; Ethereum, Arbitrum, and Polygon pinned addresses were sampled.
A2: exact custodian, vault operator, bar allocation, insurance, reserve audit cadence, and reporting committee/quorum were not verified from gold-specific official documents.
A3: live oftContract address was not read because direct read-API URLs for L2 proxies were rejected and explorer read tabs rendered dynamic values as loading.
A4: legal ownership chain from tokenholder to specific bars was not reconstructed because gold-specific pages rendered JavaScript-only shells.
A6: if off-chain attestations, insurance, or redemption contingencies exist, their live status was not verified.
A8: exact cross-chain messaging provider / relayer set was not fully verified from primary docs.
A9: no timelock or exit window for setOFTContract was verified.

headline: Ordinary transfer access is open until blocklisting, but the contract has an owner-controlled on-chain blocklist that can prevent transfers and lead to burned balances.

findings.text: No allowlist/KYC modifier was found on ordinary transfer, but transferFrom is onlyNotBlocked and _beforeTokenTransfer blocks transfers from blocked addresses unless owner.
No off-chain operator approval is needed for an ordinary unblocked ERC-20 transfer; OFT authorization is separate cross-chain mint/burn admission.
Tether web/legal pages state jurisdictional, U.S.-person, sanctions, service-restriction, freeze, and blacklist policies; these are context, not the grade driver.
Independent direct-contract access exists through Etherscan Read/Write and Read/Write as Proxy tabs.
Contract-level blocklist tooling exists: owner-only addToBlockedList/removeFromBlockedList update isBlocked, and destroyBlockedFunds can burn blocked balances.
Read access is public; write access is permissionless only for unblocked transfers, while mint/redeem/blocklist/burn are owner-only.
General Tether legal pages include sanctions/restriction clauses; gold-specific ToS extraction failed and the general page says it excludes gold.tether.to sub-pages.

steelman.red: The contract itself has an owner-controlled blocklist gating transfers and can burn blocked balances.
steelman.orange: Unblocked users can transfer via wallets/explorer without the official UI, so the official frontend/legal posture alone would not block access.
steelman.green: Green would require no contract-level whitelist/KYC/blocklist and no operator approval for entry/exit; the fetched code fails that.

rationale.verdict: Choosing red because access restriction is enforced in the deployed token code, not merely the official frontend: owner-controlled blocklisting can prevent transfers and owner can burn blocked balances.

evidence.shows: Source shows isBlocked, onlyNotBlocked, owner-only blocklist functions, _beforeTokenTransfer transfer blocking, and destroyBlockedFunds.
Ethereum surfacer lists public transfer methods and privileged blocklist/burn/mint/redeem methods.
Etherscan exposes direct Read/Write and proxy interaction tabs.
Tether states platform restrictions for listed jurisdictions and U.S. persons unless Eligible Contract Participants.
General Tether legal terms include prohibited-person, sanctions, VPN-circumvention, suspension/termination, freeze, and blacklist language, while excluding gold.tether.to sub-pages.
Protocol info: XAUt provides ownership of real physical gold; TVL by chain; TVL = total XAUt minted.
Tether bug-bounty / disclosure page.

unknowns: A1: every listed-chain deployment was not fully grepped; conclusion is based on pinned Ethereum, Arbitrum, and Polygon surfaces.
A2: cross-chain admission through OFT messaging was not fully reconstructed because live oftContract was not read.
A3: runtime IP geoblocking or wallet screening on gold.tether.to was not verified because the site rendered as a JavaScript-only shell.
A3b: no third-party frontend, SDK, wallet integration, or aggregator path was exhaustively enumerated beyond direct block-explorer/generic contract access.
A6: gold-specific ToS clause text could not be extracted verbatim from https://gold.tether.to/legal/termsofservice.

headline: Main proxy and implementation bytecode are verified on explorers, but the pinned context has no public source repo and no audit links; checked explorers report no submitted contract audits.

findings.text: Ethereum, Arbitrum, and Polygon proxy/implementation surfaces checked are explorer-verified or similar-match for standard proxy code; implementations are separately visible/resolved.
No canonical public source-code repository was pinned, and no commit SHA was established.
The protocol context contains no audit_links; checked Etherscan/Arbiscan/PolygonScan pages report No Contract Security Audit Submitted.
No recognized Solidity auditor report covering current deployed contracts was verified.
Post-audit drift could not be assessed because no audit baseline or canonical repo commit was verified; downgrade is absence of audit/repo evidence, not sampled drift.
Proxy/implementation pairing was checked: Ethereum resolves to 0x4C0d2c74..., Arbitrum to 0x9001dbe4..., and PolygonScan shows 0x6D205337... as implementation.

steelman.red: No public repo and no audit links mean outsiders cannot tie deployed bytecode to a maintained reviewed codebase, despite explorer verification.
steelman.orange: Explorer verification and proxy/implementation resolution make it better than opaque bytecode.
steelman.green: Green would require verified bytecode plus matching public repo and a recognized audit covering current deployments; not evidenced.

rationale.verdict: Choosing red because explorer verification exists, but no public GitHub repository or audit links were pinned/found and checked explorer pages report no submitted contract security audits.
